# @weight 1

busybox's ed (editors/ed.c).  Every expectation is busybox's own output,
from a busybox built from its source, run as an ordinary user.  A `|`
marks the end of each line written to standard output; `after:` is what a
command run after shows.

## the fixtures

### the files, which busybox made, and a run of ed in a fresh directory

`a.txt` holds five lines, `nonl.txt` two, the last without a newline,
`ctl.txt` a tab, a bell and a byte past 127, `long.txt` thirty lines.  Each
run is in `/tmp/x-cu-ed/w`, made afresh from them: PRE runs before ed and
writes the commands to `s`, which is its standard input, and POST runs after
it, both through the shell.

```cu
(do (proc-run (list "/bin/sh" "-c" "rm -rf /tmp/x-cu-ed && mkdir -p /tmp/x-cu-ed/w")) (def ed-f (fn (_ n) (string-append "/tmp/x-cu-ed/" n))) (file-write-all (ed-f "fx.b64") "") (proc-run (list "/bin/sh" "-c" "cd /tmp/x-cu-ed && base64 -d < fx.b64 > fx.tar")) (def ed-home (Sys getcwd)) (def ed-sh (fn (_ cmd out) (proc-run (list "/bin/sh" "-c" (string-concat (list "cd /tmp/x-cu-ed/w && { " cmd "; } > " out " 2>&1")))))) (def ed-in (fn (_ name) (if (string=? name "-") "" (let ((fd (file-open-read (string-append "/tmp/x-cu-ed/w/" name))) (buf (%str-make-raw 65536))) (let ((n (File read fd buf 65536))) (do (file-close fd) (pair buf n))))))) (def ed-norm (fn (_ f) (do (proc-run (list "/bin/sh" "-c" (string-concat (list "sed -E 's#[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}#TIME#' " f " > " f ".n")))) (file-read-all (string-append f ".n"))))) (def ed-shown (fn (_ mode) (if (string=? mode "x") (do (proc-run (list "/bin/sh" "-c" "od -An -v -tx1 /tmp/x-cu-ed/o | tr -d ' \\n' | fold -w 64 > /tmp/x-cu-ed/hex; echo >> /tmp/x-cu-ed/hex")) (file-read-all (ed-f "hex"))) (Str8 replace "\n" "|\n" (ed-norm (ed-f "o")))))) (def ed-case (fn (_ fresh in pre post mode argv) (do (if fresh (ed-sh "cd /tmp/x-cu-ed && rm -rf w && mkdir w && cd w && tar xf ../fx.tar" "/dev/null") ()) (if (string=? pre "@") () (ed-sh pre "/dev/null")) (def ed-stdin (ed-in in)) (Sys chdir "/tmp/x-cu-ed/w") (sys-dup2 1 9) (sys-dup2 2 8) (def st (let ((oo (file-open-write (ed-f "o"))) (ee (file-open-write (ed-f "e")))) (do (sys-dup2 oo 1) (sys-dup2 ee 2) (def rs (cu-run argv ed-stdin)) (sys-dup2 9 1) (sys-dup2 8 2) (file-close oo) (file-close ee) rs))) (Sys chdir ed-home) (display (string-concat (list (ed-shown mode) "stderr:\n" (file-read-all (ed-f "e")) "status " (%cu-int->str st) "\n" (if (string=? post "@") "" (do (ed-sh post (ed-f "p")) (string-append "after:\n" (file-read-all (ed-f "p"))))))))))) (display "made"))
```
---
    made

## reading and printing

### a file is read and its bytes said; p prints a range, the last line printed the current one; a line with no newline is printed as it is

```cu
(do (ed-case #t "s" "printf '1,$p\\n.=\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "a.txt")) (ed-case #t "s" "printf ',p\\n$=\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "nonl.txt")))
```
---
```output
24|
one|
two|
three|
four|
five|
5|
stderr:
status 0
10|
first|
last2|
stderr:
status 0
```

### -s says nothing of the bytes; -p PROMPT is written before each command read

```cu
(do (ed-case #t "s" "printf '2p\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "-s" "a.txt")) (ed-case #t "s" "printf '2p\\nq\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "-p" "*" "a.txt")))
```
---
```output
two|
stderr:
status 0
24|
two|
stderr:
**status 0
```

### addresses: numbers, ., $, sums and differences, a search, a mark; a bare address prints that line; an empty command moves on and prints

```cu
(do (ed-case #t "s" "printf '$-1p\\n.+0p\\n2\\n\\n\\n/fi/p\\n2ka\\n$\\n'\"'\"'ap\\n/nope/p\\n//p\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "a.txt")) (ed-case #t "s" "printf '3,p\\n,2p\\n4,2p\\n9p\\n0p\\n'\"'\"'zp\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "a.txt")))
```
---
```output
24|
four|
four|
two|
three|
four|
five|
five|
two|
stderr:
ed: can't find string "nope"
ed: can't find string "nope"
status 0
24|
three|
four|
five|
one|
two|
stderr:
ed: bad line range for print
ed: bad line range for print
ed: bad line range for print
ed: bad line range for print
status 0
```

### l shows control bytes and high ones, and each line's end

```cu
(ed-case #t "s" "printf ',l\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "ctl.txt"))
```
---
```output
21|
tab^Ihere$|
bell^G$|
highM-i$|
stderr:
status 0
```

### = says a line number, . with none the current line; - and an empty command step back and on

```cu
(ed-case #t "s" "printf '=\\n3=\\n.\\n-\\n-\\n\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "a.txt"))
```
---
```output
24|
5|
3|
five|
four|
three|
four|
stderr:
status 0
```

## editing

### a appends after a line, i inserts before it, c changes a range; a line of . ends the text, as does the end of input

```cu
(ed-case #t "s" "printf '2a\\nnew A\\nnew B\\n.\\n1i\\nfirst!\\n.\\n4,5c\\nchanged\\n.\\n,p\\n$a\\ntail' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "a.txt"))
```
---
```output
24|
first!|
one|
two|
changed|
three|
four|
five|
stderr:
status 0
```

### d deletes a range, the line after it current

```cu
(ed-case #t "s" "printf '2,3d\\n.p\\n$d\\n.p\\n,p\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "a.txt"))
```
---
```output
24|
five|
four|
one|
four|
stderr:
status 0
```

### s replaces a string, not a pattern: the first in each line, or all with g; p prints the lines changed; an empty string is the last one searched for

```cu
(do (ed-case #t "s" "printf '1,3s/e/E/\\n,p\\n,s/o/0/gp\\n/f/\\n,s//F/\\n,p\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "a.txt")) (ed-case #t "s" "printf 's\\n2s/x/y/\\n2s/t/T/q\\n2s t T \\n2s/t\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "a.txt")))
```
---
```output
24|
onE|
two|
thrEe|
four|
five|
0nE|
tw0|
f0ur|
f0ur|
0nE|
tw0|
thrEe|
F0ur|
five|
stderr:
status 0
24|
stderr:
ed: bad delimiter for substitute
ed: no substitutions found for "x"
ed: unknown option for substitute
ed: bad delimiter for substitute
ed: missing 2nd delimiter for substitute
status 0
```

## files

### w writes the buffer, or a range, and says the bytes; f says or sets the name; r reads a file in after a line

```cu
(ed-case #t "s" "printf '2,3w part\\n$r part\\n,p\\nf\\nf other\\nw\\nf\\n' > s" "cat part; echo ==; cat other" "-" (list "ed" "a.txt"))
```
---
```output
24|
10|
10|
one|
two|
three|
four|
five|
two|
three|
"a.txt"|
34|
"other"|
stderr:
status 0
after:
two
three
==
one
two
three
four
five
two
three
```

### a file that is not there ends ed at once; with no file, w wants a name; r wants one too

```cu
(do (ed-case #t "s" "printf ',p\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "nope.txt")) (ed-case #t "s" "printf 'a\\nhello\\n.\\nw\\nr\\nr nope\\nw new.txt\\n' > s" "cat new.txt" "-" (list "ed")))
```
---
```output
stderr:
ed: nope.txt: No such file or directory
status 0
6|
stderr:
ed: no file name specified
ed: no file name
ed: nope: No such file or directory
status 0
after:
hello
```

### q asks first when the buffer is changed, and a line not starting y keeps it; a q with an address or a word is refused

```cu
(do (ed-case #t "s" "printf '1d\\nq\\nn\\n,p\\nq\\ny\\n,p\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "a.txt")) (ed-case #t "s" "printf '1q\\nq x\\nq\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "a.txt")))
```
---
```output
24|
two|
three|
four|
five|
stderr:
Really quit? Really quit? status 0
24|
stderr:
ed: bad quit command
ed: bad quit command
status 0
```

### a command ed does not have, and a bad mark

```cu
(ed-case #t "s" "printf 'x\\nkA\\n'\"'\"'Ap\\n.,.p\\n' > s" "@" "-" (list "ed" "a.txt"))
```
---
```output
24|
five|
stderr:
ed: unimplemented command
ed: bad mark name
ed: bad mark name
status 0
```
